title: Agents, Tools and the Loop
summary: An agent is a language model placed inside a loop: it reads the situation, decides on an action, calls a tool, reads the result and goes round again until it decides it is done. This lesson builds that loop from messages up and puts numbers on how many steps and tokens a run costs.
objectives: After this lesson you can describe an agent as a policy inside an observe, think, act loop and draw it as a state machine
Write out the exact message sequence of a tool call and its result
Compute the expected number of steps of a run from a per-step finish probability and a step cap
Estimate the token cost of a multi-step run and explain why it grows faster than linearly
Implement a minimal agent loop with a step limit and tool dispatch
prerequisites: You should know what a prompt and a completion are and how tokens are priced ([/learn/model-foundations/tokenization](/learn/model-foundations/tokenization)). Tool definitions are introduced in [/learn/prompt-and-context/tools-and-functions](/learn/prompt-and-context/tools-and-functions); this lesson recaps what it needs.
